title: Synthetic Readers

spine.markdown: The system has undergone tuning and alpha testing by using synthetic (AI-powered) readers, which work through the text as human readers would, offering questions and comments. Each reader has been given their own profile. Such characterization of AI agents is a growing practice (Park et al. 2023; Argyle et al. 2023; Hämäläinen, Tavast, and Kunnari 2023; Masera 2026).

The Intertext system of characterization was derived from Freeman (2026). There are currently five profiles: general, collaborative, curious, skeptical, and student. The readers are powered by a different model (OpenAI GPT 5.6 terra), while the texts are generated by Claude Sonnet as noted above. The resultant readings (text and responses) may then be examined by a separate Claude agent and by the human author to evaluate the flow of the argument, the use of fund materials, links and graphics, and the quality of the prose.

These synthetic readers have shown that the model can absorb the argument of the text and apply it to new issues or examples raised by readers’ questions. The reader system has also helped the author to rethink the original argument and its evidence. For example, in The Digital Plenitude, some readers objected to the text’s formulation that traditional hierarchies in arts and culture have “almost, but not quite, vanished.” The system then drafted a more nuanced version. If this objection had occurred during a run with human readers, the spine or fund could have been changed for subsequent readers. The synthetic readings also suggested stylistic improvements to reduce the awkward wordings such as “the text claims.”

fundEntries.title: Why the reader comes from another company
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks why the synthetic readers use a different model from the text.
fundEntries.markdown:
The text is written by Anthropic's Claude and the reader is played by an OpenAI model, so that the two roles are never
one model talking to itself. The synthetic reader drives the same reading endpoint a person's browser uses.

fundEntries.title: What the synthetic reader can see
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks whether the synthetic readers have access to the author's text or the instructions.
fundEntries.markdown:
A synthetic reader sees what a person sees: the contents, each section's opening box and the conversation so far. It
never sees the instructions, the section files or the fund. The harness reads the titles and boxes from the reader's
page itself, so the reader cannot be given anything the page does not show.

fundEntries.title: The five readers
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks what the profiles are or how they differ.
fundEntries.markdown:
The curious reader is a nonspecialist who follows closely and asks for clarification. The skeptical reader is an
academic in a neighbouring field who notices unsupported claims and asks for evidence and counterexamples. The
collaborative reader wants the work to be stronger and attends to prose and movement. The general reader is the
educated reader the work is written for, who reads for the argument and writes a few plain sentences. The student is an
undergraduate with the reading assigned, who asks what terms mean and says the argument back to check it. Some may
search the web, at most twice a turn, and must name what they found.

fundEntries.title: What a synthetic reader does each turn
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how a synthetic reader decides what to do, or what is recorded.
fundEntries.markdown:
Each turn the synthetic reader chooses one action: send a message, press Return, move to another section, or finish.
It also writes a private reflection, rating its understanding, confusion and interest and adding a sentence or two of
explanation. The reflection goes into the transcript and is never sent to the text. The transcript also keeps each
reply's draft beside its revision.

fundEntries.title: How a round of readings is measured
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how the synthetic readings are evaluated, or what is counted.
fundEntries.markdown:
A report on each round counts the words of every reply and how many exceed the limit, the notes per reply, the replies
in which the text speaks of its own argument, phrases repeated between replies and closing sentences used more than
once, the readers' private ratings, how many revisions were applied, and the share of the prompt read from the cache.
A separate count compares the replies' absolutes, hedges and closing formulas with the author's own prose. The counts
say how the prose sounds, not whether a claim is right.

fundEntries.title: The blind judge
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how one version of the system is compared with another.
fundEntries.markdown:
To compare versions of the system, a separate Claude agent reads replies from several rounds shuffled together and
unlabelled, and answers the same questions of each, without knowing which version produced which reply. A key kept
apart from the judge then sorts the verdicts by round. The author reads the transcripts with the judge's report and the
counts, and decides what to change.

fundEntries.title: A loop for revising the work
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how the synthetic readings feed back into the text.
fundEntries.markdown:
The readings are an editorial instrument, not only a software test. Comparable sessions are run on a known edition and
section; the transcripts and private reflections are read across profiles; an editorial hypothesis is formed rather
than treating any one reply as a verdict; the author's text, the section boundaries, the boxes or the instructions are
revised as the evidence warrants; and the same conditions are run again. Synthetic runs never change the published
text: a preview of how the editor would evolve a section from a reading is never published.

fundEntries.title: What synthetic readers cannot show
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks whether synthetic readers can stand in for people.
fundEntries.markdown:
A simulated reader argues from the text's own terms more than a person does, and it has no lived experience to bring.
The readings find assumptions, overstatements, repetition and gaps. They cannot show how real readers understand or
respond, and they are no substitute for testing with people.

fundEntries.title: Experiments with the fund
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how the effect of the fund can be tested.
fundEntries.markdown:
Two experimental editions, used only by the synthetic readers, give the text the spine alone or the spine with the fund,
with web search off and no outside examples, so that the availability of the fund is the only difference between them.
They show whether and how the text draws on optional material when it has it.

changeSummary: Structural package of the DH2027 paper (H-001): one passage per paragraph of the paper, the paper's prose unchanged apart from its figure references. Fund entries drafted from the InterText documentation by a Claude session (2026-11-25), approved by Jay and accepted, 2026-11-25.
